edition: Issue #012 - A marathon decided by scissors, a pub birthday for the nation, and a 1m state visit with a bang
tagline: Your 3-minute break. Zero fluff, maximum banter.

stories.headline: London Marathon big schedule call was settled by rock-paper-scissors - and the sub-2hr man lost
stories.summary: Next year's two-day London Marathon decided which elite races run on which day via a best-of-one game of rock-paper-scissors between the marathon world record-holder and the women's wheelchair record-holder.

body.text: The schedule for next year's special two-day London Marathon was decided by something conspicuously low-tech: a game of rock-paper-scissors. Organisers said the battle was between Kenya's Sabastian Sawe, who became the first man to run a sub-two-hour marathon in a record-eligible race, finishing the 2026 London course in 1:59:30, and women's wheelchair record-holder Catherine Debrunner. Sawe lost, which meant the traditional Sunday slot was reserved for the women's elite and wheelchair races, with the men's races on Saturday 24 April. The 2027 edition is being split across two days as a one-off to put an even brighter spotlight on the athletes, and a record 1.33 million people have entered the public ballot.

Sport's most decorated marathon fields, one of the biggest events in the world, and the schedule that decides who runs in front of the global lens, all riding on a game children settle to decide who has to go to the school fair. Rock beat scissors, the record-holder saw, and a feud began. Honestly it is the most honest decision-making process in elite sport all year: no committees, no TV money, no stakeholder consultation. Just two of the fastest humans on the planet squaring off like they are choosing teams for lunch. Sabastian will be fine. If he has to run a day earlier, he has a whole extra 24 hours to think about how the scissors won.

Reuters via RNZ (1 Oct 2026): The 2027 London Marathon will be a one-off two-day event. The elite-race schedule was decided by a game of rock-paper-scissors between Kenyan Sabastian Sawe (2026 men's champion; first sub-two-hour marathon in a record-eligible race, 1:59:30) and women's wheelchair record-holder Catherine Debrunner. Sawe lost, so the women's elite and wheelchair races keep the traditional Sunday slot and the men's races run Saturday 24 April. A record 1.33 million people entered the public ballot.

stories.headline: Everyone is invited to Sir Dave Dobbyn's 70th - the party is a pub on the Coromandel
stories.summary: Sir Dave Dobbyn turns 70 on 3 January and will mark it with a one-off summer show at the Coroglen Tavern, with tickets on sale 6 October.

body.text: Sir Dave Dobbyn will celebrate his 70th birthday with a show at the Coroglen Tavern, telling fans for the good people of the Coromandel there is nowhere he would rather be on his 70th birthday. The one-off summer gig falls on Sunday 3 January, fresh off his set at Rhythm and Vines. He will be supported by Christchurch indie-rock singer-songwriter Mim Jensen and rising alt-rocker Sam Cullen and His Band from Southland. General public tickets go on sale Tuesday 6 October at 10am, and, in true invitation-to-the-whole-nation style, everyone is welcome.

Most 70th birthday parties are a strained gathering of relatives in a hall you would never choose. Sir Dave is having his at a legendary country pub, and every single person in the country is invited. That is the closest any of us will get to being on the guest list for an event that is basically the Coromandel doing its version of a state banquet, except the dress code is jandals and the national anthem is Slice of Heaven sung loudly and wrong. He has spent a lifetime writing songs that feel like they belong to whoever is listening, so inviting everyone to his birthday is just him doing the same thing out loud. Clear the calendar, warm up your best falsetto, and may whoever is in charge of the beer order have a bit of a think before pouring.

RNZ Life (30 Sep 2026): Sir Dave Dobbyn turns 70 on 3 January and will play a one-off 70th-birthday show at the Coroglen Tavern (Coromandel) on Sunday 3 January, after his set at Rhythm and Vines. Supporting acts are Mim Jensen and Sam Cullen and His Band. General public tickets go on sale Tuesday 6 October at 10am. RNZ reported Sir Dave was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 2022 and has since been writing new music with his son.

stories.headline: The 1 million state visit: what Modi's two-day trip actually cost NZ agencies
stories.summary: Documents obtained under the OIA show Government agencies spent a combined $1,021,168.93 on the Indian PM's two-day visit in July, including $4,336.18 on ammunition for the gun salute.

body.text: Government agencies spent more than 1 million dollars on Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's two-day state visit in July, according to documents obtained by RNZ under the Official Information Act. Tallying figures from six agencies, Internal Affairs, Police, Defence Force, the PM's department, Trade and Enterprise and Foreign Affairs, RNZ put the combined bill at $1,021,168.93. The biggest outlay was the Department of Internal Affairs at $638,309, followed by Police at $217,515. The visit, which included a major Auckland security operation, ended with New Zealand and India elevating their relationship to a strategic partnership and agreeing a roadmap to 2030.

Nothing says warm bilateral relations like a line item for $4,336.18 of ammunition purely so the visiting dignitary's arrival can be marked by loud, expensive bangs. Is it a state visit or a really committed fireworks display? Between that and a 1,200-dollar towing bill the agencies clearly did not cap the hospitality tab. We are not here to begrudge diplomacy, the roadmap to 2030 sounds lovely, but somewhere between 126 thousand dollars of audio-visual production and a 245-thousand-dollar gala there is a reminder that in line with expectations is how a department says we honestly do not know. Still, if a whisper of Sir Dave's birthday gig up the road needed any of that million, we have an idea for resourcing it better.

RNZ (Blessen Tom, 1 Oct 2026, via OIA): six agencies incurred a combined $1,021,168.93 for Modi's two-day visit (11 July 2026). Department of Internal Affairs: $638,309 (general operating $293,698; government hospitality incl. NZ-India business event, Winning Partnership gala and Goldmine Innovation Experience $244,983; accommodation, meals and travel $53,759; transport $31,141; domestic travel $14,728). NZ Police: $217,515 as of 28 Aug (constabulary allowances $83,956.90; flights $71,671; accommodation $34,561.60; vehicle rentals $16,277.16; venue hire $6,764.28; a $1,200 towing bill). NZ Trade and Enterprise: $131,479 (audio-visual and production $126,269). NZ Defence Force: $30,338.66 incl. $4,336.18 for ammunition for the gun salute. DPMC: $2,042.54. MFAT: $1,484.73 on gifts (three Matariki candle sets $883.98; two signed first editions of Edmund Hillary's From the Ocean to the Sky $342; custom book box $258.75). The community event at Spark Arena was funded by money raised by the Indian community in NZ.

affiliate_cta.headline: Planning a big event of your own? Here's where we'd look.
affiliate_cta.body: Whether you are booking your Coromandel birthday bash, training for a sub-2 hour marathon, or somehow in charge of a state visit's catering, a couple of harmless starting points never went astray. No pressure, no commitment, and sadly no rock-paper-scissors involved.
